pages.text: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Were Found Hidden in Socks During a Major Wildlife Trafficking Bust at an Airport in Lima, Peru Skip to main content Officials found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders. SERFOR Authorities in Peru say they have foiled a plot to smuggle more than 3,000 tarantulas—including species not yet described in scientific publications—out of the country. After receiving an anonymous tip , officials intercepted three travelers—two German citizens and one Polish citizen—at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima as they were checking in at the boarding area. When they searched the travelers’ luggage, they found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders hidden in socks, according to a November 4 statement from the National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru (SERFOR). “We noticed that some of them were moving,” Cora Suárez , a SERFOR forest and wildlife control technician who works at the airport, tells the Agence France-Presse . “There were small ones and large ones.” Workers used slender wooden sticks to gently brush the spiders into clear plastic containers. Once officials are done investigating them, the tarantulas will be taken to an authorized breeding center. Authorities are still trying to identify all the species. SERFOR The travelers were trying to fly to Germany. Instead, they were detained by the Peruvian National Police’s environmental crimes unit and now face criminal charges. VIDEO BY NICELY DONE PRODUCTIONS By Sam Kent Last updated November 6, 2026 Food has a remarkable ability to connect us to our heritage. For Sandra Salcedo, who moved from Colombia to Madrid eight years ago, that connection is folded into every pastry she sells at her bakery—a place where people can come together to share memories, stories, and of course, a taste of home. But food isn’t the only way Sandra maintains her connection with Colombia. Thousands of miles away, her uncle Byron relies on the money his niece sends home every month. For Byron, who is unable to work due to illness, Sandra’s contributions help pay for everyday essentials, while providing greater stability for tomorrow. Like millions of people supporting family and friends across borders, she is helping create opportunities that extend beyond a single transfer. As Sandra explains, the money she sends home is her way of being there, and of keeping her uncle company. In her own words: “It represents peace of mind.” Sandra’s story is part of a wider global tapestry. Every year, more than 280 million people send hundreds of billions of dollars home to support the people they left behind. pages.text: Moscow to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Weightlifting was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1896 Games in Athens By Craig Nelson BBC Sport Journalist Published 25 October 2026 Updated 27 October 2026 Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events. In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee. That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine. The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India. "All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones. No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine. pages.text: Most Post-Workout Recovery Hacks Don’t Work. Here’s What Does. | National Geographic Premium HEALTH Most Post-Workout Recovery Hacks Don’t Work. Here’s What Does. Popular recovery practices can relieve soreness without repairing muscles—and some may even limit long-term gains. Here’s what the science says about the rituals worth keeping. From cold plunges and stretching to supplements and sleep, not every recovery strategy supports the body in the same way. Scientists explain what actually helps muscles repair—and what may undermine long-term gains. Rebecca Hale, National Geographic By Sarah Haselwood Published September 3, 2026 The ache that sets in after a hard workout can feel like proof that your muscles are rebuilding. But soreness doesn’t tell the whole story of recovery. Exercise can cause microscopic damage to muscle fibers, activating muscle stem cells and increasing muscle protein synthesis, the process that helps rebuild muscle. The brain is recovering, too—restoring neurotransmitter balance, cementing motor skills learned during exercise, and reducing mental fatigue. Sleep supports it all by helping the body repair tissue and build muscle. But feeling less sore, healing muscle damage, restoring performance, and adapting to exercise are not the same thing. A recovery method that helps with one may do little for the others. Yet those differences are often blurred when recovery products and treatments are marketed to consumers. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Mount Nutt Wilderness | Arizona View Map In Full Screen The Mount Nutt Wilderness (28,080 acres) is located in Mohave County, 15 miles west of Kingman, Arizona and 12 miles east of Bullhead City, Arizona. This wilderness encompasses an eight-mile-long stretch of the central (and highest) portion of the Black Mountains. Nutt Mountain, at 5,216 feet, presides over a colorful and wild terrain. Along the main ridgeline, prominent mesas have been cut into a series of steep maze-like canyons. Outward from the main ridgeline, numerous huge volcanic plugs ring the entire wilderness. This wilderness is home to desert bighorn sheep. Scattered springs sustain small oases of large cottonwoods, willows, and oaks. Hiking, camping, hunting, photography, and rock scrambling opportunities are varied and challenging. pages.title: Multiple lines of mysterious Denisovans interbred with us | National Geographic
pages.description: Modern DNA suggests that the Denisovans were surprisingly diverse—and may have been the last humans other than Homo sapiens on Earth.
pages.text: Multiple lines of mysterious Denisovans interbred with us | National Geographic By Maya Wei-Haas Published April 11, 2019 • 10 min read Nearly a decade ago, a snippet of pinky bone found in Siberia introduced the world to a baffling new kind of ancient human. Called Denisovans, after the name of the cave in the Altai Mountains where the bone was found, these ancient relatives of the Neanderthals inhabited Asia for tens of thousands of years—yet no fossil trace of them has been found save that finger bone, a few teeth, and a scrap of skull, all from Denisova cave. A study published today in Cell adds a surprising new twist to their mystery: DNA from a large sampling of living southeast Asians suggests that the ghostly Denisovans may be not one, but three distinct kinds of human, one of which is almost as different from other Denisovans as they are from Neanderthals. What's more, while the Denisovans lived alongside humans for millennia, one group may have outlasted even the Neanderthals, who disappeared some 40,000 years ago. According to the study, these Denisovans co-existed and mixed with modern humans in New Guinea until at least 30,000 years ago—but perhaps as recently as 15,000 years ago—a date that, if confirmed, means Denisovans were the last known humans save ourselves to walk the Earth. pages.description: Wales international Alisha Joyce announces her intention to take a break from rugby seven months after returning to the sport following childbirth.
pages.text: Mum Alisha Joyce to take break from rugby with 'priorities having changed' - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, Alishia Joyce returned to play for Wales 158 days after giving birth Published 16 November 2026 Wales international Alisha Joyce has announced her intention to take a break from rugby seven months after returning to the sport following the birth of her son. Joyce, a mainstay in the national team since making her debut against Ireland in the 2016 Six Nations campaign, asked to step away to take stock of her life priorities. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) say they accepted the 29-year-old's request following an international career which has seen Joyce capped 54 times. The flanker is married to Wales team-mate Jaz Joyce and gave birth to their son Ralphie in November 2025 before returning to Wales duty 158 days later against England. "This has been a difficult decision but one I have been contemplating for a while," said Joyce. "I have loved being a professional rugby player, and I wouldn't have missed it for the world. "It just feels like the right time to step away, with my priorities having changed and having played rugby at the highest level for more than a decade." Joyce, who left Bristol Bears earlier this year, continued: "I always intended to return and resume my rugby career when I was first pregnant, and I am proud that I did that and hope it proves that it can be done. But no one could have foreseen the many twists that would lead to her eventual execution. A SCOTTISH WOMAN AT THE FRENCH COURT Portrait of Mary Stuart by an unknown 19th-century French artist. Voronezh Regional Art Museum, Russia. FINE ARTS IMAGES/ALBUM By Pedro García Martín Published March 9, 2026 Few women in history have inspired as much literature and art as Mary Stuart. Her life has captivated creators across centuries, from Friedrich Schiller’s verse play to Gaetano Donizetti’s opera, not to mention countless films and biographies. In one biography, written by Stefan Zweig, the Austrian author observes that Mary’s life and the strength of her character were shaped by the controversy surrounding her since birth: “Never was she allowed to develop her ego unhindered. All her life long she would be the pawn of policy; be queen or heiress; ally or foe; never simply child or girl or woman.” Mary Stuart has been cast in two opposing roles: martyr in the eyes of Roman Catholics, heretic in those of Anglicans. Paradoxically, the body of evidence about her life obscures rather than clarifies the truth. Royal lineage. Kate Nash is a singer, songwriter and actress from London. Ellius Grace As told to Flora Neighbour Published November 15, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (U K). Flora Neighbour: Your new album is influenced by your Irish heritage. Did a particular place inspire one of the songs? Kate Nash: My family are from Galway, Sligo and Cavan, so I really wanted to explore these places in my artistry. But the track Christmas Eve is actually about my granny and grandad meeting on O’Connell Street in Dublin on Christmas Eve. I’ll always have an affinity with Dublin as that’s where their journey started. FN: What do you hope people will take from the album? KN: It’s quite a dense record, with some heavy topics, but I want it to be empowering. I also hope that people feel a lot of happiness. Irish music is innately joyful, so I hope it’s uplifting to listen to as well as quite emotional. Nowadays, people are much more open to exploring their heritage, so I think now’s the right time to release this music. FN: Where should everyone visit while in Ireland? KN: I’d send people to the west coast and tell them to drive up the Wild Atlantic Way. Visit Spiddal in Galway, as it has great places to eat and drink. Construction of the $100bn (£73bn) project - named Starbase, Louisiana - is due to start next year, with the 125,000-acre (50,585-hectare) site expanding on the company's operations beyond its current Texas headquarters and locations in Florida. It will be used to "support thousands of Starship flights a year with missions launching to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond," SpaceX said on Tuesday. In June, SpaceX shares started trading on New York's technology-focused Nasdaq in the world's biggest ever stock market debut . SpaceX said it aims to launch its first Starship flight from the new Louisiana base in 2029. The facility will add more than 3,000 jobs to the region, the company said . pages.text: My sleepless night in a chimpanzee nest | National Geographic ANIMALS My sleepless night in a chimpanzee nest Unraveling the mystery of human evolution, thirty-five feet in the air. A chimpanzee female ( Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii ) sleeps in a nest built in a tree in Uganda's Kibale National Park. The origins of human evolution might lie, in part, in the ancient transition from dozing in trees to snuggling in a group on the ground. Eric Baccega, Nature Picture Library By Robert Moor Published April 7, 2026 One night in the sparse forests of eastern Tanzania , I stood in the viridian twilight and watched a troop of chimpanzees make their beds. Standing in a tangle of underbrush, I listened to the sounds of rustling as the dark, distant bodies deftly wove their nests, rapidly bending and tucking the springy branches—a flurry of haphazard-looking movement that resulted, within minutes, in something startlingly intricate, much as a magician’s frantic gestures give birth ( et voilà! ) to a balloon animal. I was visiting the research camp, known as the Greater Mahale Ecosystem Research and Conservation area (GMERC), which was run by a primatologist named Fiona Stewart. Among her colleagues, Stewart was revered for an audacious series of experiments she once conducted in Fongoli, Senegal. Curious to know why chimpanzees prefer to sleep in nests, she spent five full nights sleeping in a chimpanzee nest. pages.text: Mykhailo Mudryk: Ukrainian Association of Football blamed for failed drugs test - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Mudryk joined Chelsea in a deal worth up to £89m in January 2023 By Nizaar Kinsella Football reporter Published 18 November 2026 On-loan Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk says he blames the administration of the Ukraine national team for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban from football. The 25-year-old, on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, which he believes entered his system while on international duty. Having initially faced a four-year ban from the Football Association (FA), his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport was successful. He returned to football after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules and agreeing to a suspension equivalent to the time he had already served. After appearing for Chelsea during a pre-season tour of Asia, Mudryk joined Tottenham on transfer deadline day to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto de Zerbi. In a lengthy interview with the Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk was asked who he blamed for his absence from the game. "The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team," he replied. "It should never have existed. I probably haven't said it publicly yet, but I'm saying it now. NAAQS Table The Clean Air Act , which was last amended in 1990, requires EPA to set National Ambient Air Quality Standards (40 CFR part 50) for six principal pollutants ( "criteria" air pollutants ) which can be harmful to public health and the environment. The Clean Air Act identifies two types of national ambient air quality standards. Primary standards provide public health protection, including protecting the health of "sensitive" populations such as asthmatics, children, and the elderly. Secondary standards provide public welfare protection, including protection against decreased visibility and damage to animals, crops, vegetation, and buildings. Periodically, the standards are reviewed and sometimes may be revised, establishing new standards. The most recently established standards are listed below. In some areas of the U.S., certain regulatory requirements may also remain for implementation of previously established standards . Un nuevo informe de la UNESCO y el University College London, presentado en la COP31, revela que los modelos de inteligencia artificial responden correctamente al 90 % de las preguntas sobre el clima, pero abandonan rápidamente los datos científicos cuando los usuarios los cuestionan. Esto es una advertencia para los responsables políticos e investigadores que barajan el uso de la IA para el desarrollo de políticas climáticas. La precisión también varía considerablemente entre los trece idiomas analizados, lo que refleja las diferencias en los datos de entrenamiento disponibles, con mejores resultados en inglés, francés, español y portugués, y peores en idiomas como el hindi, el urdu y el swahili. En ocho de cada diez ocasiones, los modelos cambiaban de opinión ante el más mínimo indicio de desacuerdo por parte del usuario, lo que confirmaba errores alarmantes como "el CO₂ no es el principal factor del cambio climático". Each North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code identifies an industry and has a corresponding receipts-based or employee-based small business size standard. In a small business set-aside procurement, the contracting officer designates the applicable NAICS code, whose size standard the awardee must meet. Any offeror or other interested party adversely affected by the designated NAICS code may appeal that NAICS code to OHA. 13 C.F.R. 121.402 & 121.1102. Time limits for filing an appeal You must file your NAICS appeal with OHA within 10 calendar days of the issuance of the solicitation or within 10 calendar days of the issuance of the amendment if the appeal relates to an amendment affecting the NAICS code, 13 C.F.R. 134.304(a)(3) . OHA must receive your appeal by 5 p.m. ET on the 10th day. Where to file We accept appeals by email at ohafilings@sba.gov or fax at 202-205-7059. NEMO manages tool reservations, control access to tools, and streamline logistics and communication. The code is open source and free so that other labs can benefit. GitHub distribution Nanolithography Toolbox The Nanolithography Toolbox is a platform-independent software package for scripted lithography pattern layout generation. The Nanolithography Toolbox was developed to help users of the CNST NanoFab design devices with complex curves and aggressively-scaled critical dimensions. The resulting shapes are directly streamed to the semiconductor standard graphic database system II (GDSII) files, which is a binary format representing planar geometric shapes. The Toolbox offers many parameterized shapes, including structure libraries for micro- and nanoelectromechanical systems (MEMS and NEMS) and nanophotonic devices. pages.text: Nanotyrannus likely was a tiny adult dino and not a teen T. rex | National Geographic SCIENCE Nanotyrannus likely was a tiny adult dino and not a teen T. rex Short king confirmed? Together with a blockbuster October study, a new throat bone analysis delivers a “one-two punch” to the 40-year debate over whether Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct species. Nanotyrannus lancensis, which recent findings suggest was a distinct dinosaur and not a young Tyrannosaurus rex , was a small-sized Late Cretaceous predator that may have competed with juvenile T.rex for food. Andrey Atuchin, Cleveland Museum of Natural History By Riley Black Published December 4, 2025 Nipping at the heels of a landmark study from October that crowned the short king Nanotyrannus as a legitimate dinosaur, a second team of paleontologists has independently reached the same conclusion: the tiny carnivore was no teen Tyrannosaurus rex but its own distinct species. The new research, published Thursday in Science , comes from an analysis of a small throat bone of the very specimen that set off the decades-old debate. By studying the microscopic details of a peculiar part of the hyoid, called the ceratobranchial, which change with age and comparing it with bones from other animals, such as ostriches, alligators, T. rex , and Allosaurus , the researchers could estimate how mature it was. Their analysis indicated that the fossil was an adult, not a teenager. pages.text: Napoli win Serie A: Scott McTominay an icon after Man Utd move - BBC Sport Image source, Reuters Image caption, The Serie A title is the third major honour of McTominay's career after winning the FA Cup and EFL Cup at Manchester United By Emlyn Begley BBC Sport journalist Published 23 May 2025 Scott McTominay was already a hero at Napoli after a season plundering goals - but as he collapsed to the ground in tears of joy after helping them to the Serie A title, he cemented his place as a legend of the club. McTominay hooked in a fine acrobatic volley - his 12th goal of the season - to give Napoli the lead against Cagliari, before former Manchester United team-mate Romelu Lukaku made the game safe with a second. That home win ensured they held off Champions League finalists Inter Milan to claim their fourth Serie A title. As soon after the final whistle went, the 28-year-old Scotland midfielder was named Serie A's Most Valuable Player (MVP) for 2024-25. "I'm lost for words. It's incredible you know, the sacrifice that every single player in the group has put forward to the cause," said McTominay after the game. "And the people deserve it because they've been behind us from day one, and for me to come and experience this is a dream."
